unit.title: Distance, Area and Volume
unit.blurb: Converting between miles and kilometres, areas of parallelograms and trapezia, and the volume and surface area of triangular prisms and pyramids.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Convert between miles and kilometres using 5 miles ≈ 8 km.

O2.t: Use formulae to find the area of parallelograms and trapezia.

O3.t: Calculate the volume of triangular prisms.

O4.t: Calculate the surface area of triangular prisms and pyramids from their nets.

sections.title: The area of a parallelogram and trapezium

p: **Area of a parallelogram = base × perpendicular height**. Cut off a triangle and move it: it becomes a rectangle.
Use the **perpendicular** (straight up) height, not the sloping side.
**Area of a trapezium = ½ (a + b) h**, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the height between them.

lesson.q: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm and height 4 cm.

p: Do not use the slanted side for the height.

q.prompt: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Find its area.

sections.title: Calculating the volume of triangular prisms

p: A **prism** has the same cross-section all along its length. **Volume = area of cross-section × length**.
For a triangular prism: volume = ½ × base × height × length.

lesson.q: A triangular prism has a cross-section with base 6 cm and height 4 cm. It is 10 cm long. Find its volume.

p: The triangle's area is ½ × base × height. Forgetting the ½ doubles the volume.

sections.title: Calculating the surface area of triangular prisms and pyramids

p: The **surface area** is the total area of all the faces. Draw the net and find the area of each face.
A triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles. A square-based pyramid: 1 square + 4 triangles.

lesson.q: A square-based pyramid has base 6 cm and triangular faces of height 5 cm. Find its surface area.

p: A triangular prism has 5 faces: do not forget the two triangular ends.
